newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian denied euthanasia dies after coma.
newsitem.headline: Australian denied euthanasia dies after coma.

text.p: One of two terminally ill Australians who were denied the opportunity to use a euthanasia law when it was overturned by federal parliament died on Tuesday after a four-day coma induced by drugs.

Euthanasia campaigner Dr Philip Nitschke, who helped four people die under the law in the remote Northern Territory, announced the death of 56-year-old former nursing sister Esther Wild, a cancer patient.
Nitschke told the Australian Associated Press news agency that Wild, who suffered the skin cancer carcenoid syndrome, had been finally denied her wish for a lawful quick death.
Instead she had suffered a form of "slow euthanasia" as a result of the administration of pain relieving drugs.
Wild and one other unidentified patient had completed the formal requirements of the Rights of the Terminally Ill Act when the Senate on March 26 passed legislation to quash it.
The two appealed to Governor-General Sir William Deane, Queen Elizabeth's representative in Australia, to delay signing the bill into law but Deane refused.
Nitschke said Wild had been rendered comatose on Sunday to relieve "relentless physical and emotional pain" of her illness.
She had become lucid enough to communicate with people around her on several occasions throughout her ordeal and at one stage asked a friend whether or not she was finally dead.
"We were forced to ignore Esther's final and most important wish, and I deeply resent that," Nitschke said.
"Relieving her pain in this way would be construed as 'slow' euthanasia, and this was not what the patient wanted.

"This treatment may be consistent with the principles of good palliative care, but when a patient is forced to go through this prior to death, because they are unable to get what they want, the whole exercise becomes an obscenity."
Nitschke attacked Kevin Andrews, the government backbencher who introduced the anti-euthanasia legislation to parliament.

"Kevin Andrews and the members of the Senate who voted for his bill should have been at the bedside throughout this four day ordeal to see at first hand the misery, suffering and sense of betrayal their actions brought on this terminally ill woman."
